comic.title: The Long Run
comic.premise: In 2026, an entrepreneur and tech executive goes for a routine long trail run in the forests of Vilnius. The story grows from this ordinary outing; everything else is open for the storyteller to discover coherently.

comic.title: The Familiar Trail
comic.caption: In October 2026, Mantas went into the Vilnius woods for his usual long run. During the week he built a company and led its technology team; out here, the next kilometre was enough to occupy him. He knew this path by its bends and roots. At the first climb, he slowed. A pine lay across the trail, its stump cleanly sawn. Pale sawdust still rested on the damp ground. Beyond it, two muddy tire tracks followed the narrow path into the trees. Mantas stopped beside the cut. Someone had brought machinery onto a trail he had run for years.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: That wasn't here last week.

comic.title: The Buried Wheel
comic.caption: Mantas picked his way around the pine and followed the muddy tracks. Fifty metres beyond the bend, he found their source: a green forestry tractor, its front wheel sunk deep into a wet rut, with a short trailer of cut logs behind it. The man beside it looked more embarrassed than surprised to see him. He pointed back along the trail, then at the wheel. Mantas had come out to give his mind a rest from other people's problems. He looked at the mud, the man's empty hands, and the quiet machine. His pace no longer mattered.

dialogue.speaker: Forestry worker
dialogue.text: I cut that pine this morning. Thought I could get the trailer through.

dialogue.speaker: Forestry worker
dialogue.text: Can you help me call someone?

comic.title: A Call Through the Trees
comic.caption: Mantas pulled his phone from the vest pocket and asked for the number. The man introduced himself as Jonas, then slowly recited his colleague’s digits. A faint voice answered on the second attempt. Mantas described the bend, the loaded trailer and the sunken front wheel. Jonas leaned closer, his worried expression easing as he heard the reply. Another tractor could reach them in about twenty minutes. Mantas looked at the churned-up track. His planned run could wait; for now, they had someone coming.

dialogue.speaker: Jonas
dialogue.text: Tell him we’ll wait here.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: He knows the track. About twenty minutes.

comic.title: The First Pull
comic.caption: Twenty minutes later, the low rumble of another tractor reached the bend. Jonas climbed back into his cab while his colleague attached a tow cable and took position on the firmer part of the track. Mantas put his phone away and waited on the verge. The cable tightened. For a moment the green tractor only rocked; then its muddy front wheel began to rise against the edge of the rut. Jonas held the steering wheel steady, the pine logs still upright behind him. Mantas watched the orange vest through the cab window. There was movement now, and room to let the workers finish.

comic.title: Firm Ground
comic.caption: The front wheel clears the lip of the rut. Jonas keeps the green tractor straight while his colleague draws the loaded trailer onto the firmer stretch ahead. Only when the trailer’s last wheels are clear do they stop. The tow cable falls slack against the leaves. From the open cab door, Jonas gives Mantas a relieved thumbs-up. Mantas has checked his watch; now he answers with a wave from the mossy verge. The delay has cooled his legs, and he shifts his weight, ready to start again. Behind the bend, the sawn pine still lies across the footpath.

dialogue.speaker: Jonas
dialogue.text: Thank you for staying.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Glad it worked. I’ll get moving.

comic.title: Back into Stride
comic.caption: Around the bend, Mantas finds the pine exactly where he left it. Pale sawdust lies beside the stump, and the trunk still cuts across his familiar path. He slows to a walk and follows a short strip of firm moss around the sawn end, watching where he places his feet. Beyond the timber, the trail opens again between the birches. He takes an easy first stride, letting the rhythm return. His long run has acquired an unexpected pause, a phone call and two new faces; now it has its next ordinary step.

comic.title: A Smaller Loop
comic.caption: Several minutes beyond the fallen pine, Mantas reaches the familiar fork. His breathing has settled back into its easy rhythm, but the watch brings the morning into focus: helping Jonas has used twenty minutes of the run. With his wrist still raised, he decides to take the shorter return loop on the left. The other branch climbs between roots and stones. There is no need to win the time back by pushing harder over them. The forest still offers a good run; it will simply be a smaller one today.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Short loop today.

comic.title: Back at the Edge
comic.caption: Fifteen minutes after the fork, the trees opened onto the familiar trailhead. Mantas eased into a walk, then stopped beside the low wooden railing and took a drink, his free hand resting on the damp timber. The shorter loop had brought him back without a hurried finish. His legs felt the wet ground, but his breathing was settling. The morning had cost him twenty unexpected minutes; it had also left two workers and their loaded trailer safely on firm track. He let that be enough for the moment. First, water and a quiet walk out of the trees.

comic.title: Back in Reach
comic.caption: Mantas pushes the flask back into its pocket and leaves the railing behind. A few metres farther on, the gravel widens toward the quiet street beyond the trees. His phone vibrates. It is Rūta from the company, asking whether he can join the team before noon to look through their signup flow. He keeps an easy walking pace and listens. The run is finished, even if it was shorter than planned; there is no need to hurry the last few steps. He agrees to the review and keeps walking toward the street, carrying the morning’s interruption back into an ordinary working day.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta (by phone)
dialogue.text: Can we review the signup flow before noon?

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Yes. I’ll come back and look at it with you.

comic.title: A Fresh Attempt
comic.caption: Before noon, Mantas is back at the company’s Vilnius office. His running vest hangs on the chair as he leans over the table beside Rūta. She points to the signup flow on the laptop: its second step requests the same contact details again. Rather than jumping straight to a fix, Mantas proposes following the whole route as a new visitor. The interruption in the forest has used up his spare time; this meeting will have to stay focused. They begin with the first screen.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: It asks for the same details twice.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Let’s try it from the beginning.

comic.title: Carry It Forward
comic.caption: Rūta enters a fresh set of test details and advances through signup. The next screen opens with the same fields empty. Going back, they find the original entries still sitting in the first step. The effort has been repeated because the information has not followed the visitor. Mantas watches her return to the second screen. They agree on a small, concrete change: carry the details forward, and let the next step ask only for something new. Before changing anything, Rūta will record the example so the team can reproduce it and check the result.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: It kept them back there. It just asks again here.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Carry them forward. Then test the whole path again.

comic.title: The Reproducible Case
comic.caption: Rūta records the route through signup, the empty fields they found, and what should happen instead. Beside the laptop, Mantas sketches two simple steps joined by an arrow. The details already entered belong to the same person all the way through. They add one more check: going back and forward must not lose those entries either. With the example and expected behavior written down, the problem is ready for the team to change and test. The sketch settles the intended flow; the software still needs the work.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: Steps, result, expected behavior. It’s recorded.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: And check going back, then forward again.

comic.title: The First Forward Check
comic.caption: About twenty minutes later, Mantas turns the laptop toward himself and makes the agreed change in a local preview. The second step now carries the contact details forward and leaves only the additional information to enter. Rūta watches the first forward check, comparing it with the example they recorded. The change is visible, but neither of them calls the job finished. They still need to return to the first step, move forward again, and follow the signup all the way through. Mantas keeps his hands at the keyboard while Rūta points to the remaining field.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: The details are here. Now go back.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Then forward again, with the new field filled.

comic.title: All the Way Through
comic.caption: Mantas filled the additional field, went back, and changed one contact detail. When he moved forward again, the correction followed him and the new entry was still there. Rūta compared both screens with her notes, then watched him finish the signup in the local preview. The confirmation appeared without asking for those details a second time. She recorded the result beside the original problem and its acceptance checks. The change had now survived the route a real user might take through the form; it was ready for review before release.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: The entries stayed. The whole path passed.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Save those checks with the change.

comic.title: A Second Pair of Eyes
comic.caption: Before noon, Mantas asks a teammate to give the small change a fresh look. Darius joins them at the table, examines the change and follows Rūta’s recorded steps himself. He corrects a contact detail, moves backward and forward, then completes the signup. The correction and additional entry remain where they belong. With the behavior checked independently, he gives a quiet nod. Mantas lets his shoulders drop; the morning’s detour has still left room to finish this properly. The review is complete. Release is the next step.

dialogue.speaker: Darius
dialogue.text: The change is clear, and the checks pass. Approved.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Thanks. We can move it forward.

comic.title: Into the Live Flow
comic.caption: With Darius’s review complete, Mantas releases the small change. A few minutes later, the release finishes and Rūta opens a fresh signup on the live service. She enters the contact details once, moves forward, then returns to correct one of them. On the next screen, the correction is there and the additional entry remains. The final confirmation appears without another request for the same details. Darius stays with them for the check, and Rūta points to the result beside her open notebook. The morning’s interruption has become a finished repair. Mantas rests his hands on the table, ready to leave the meeting room.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: The release is complete.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: The live check passed. We’re done.

comic.title: The Footpath
comic.caption: With the live signup checked, the meeting breaks up. Rūta closes the laptop and Darius heads out. Mantas gathers his vest from the chair and retrieves his phone. The morning has left one practical question unanswered: the pine still lies across a route he knows other runners use. He calls Jonas. The worker says they are cutting the trunk into sections now that the tractor is free, and promises to call when the footpath is clear. Mantas thanks him. The office repair is finished; the woodland job is still underway. For now, he will keep using the safe way around the cut end.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: How is the footpath looking?

dialogue.speaker: Jonas
dialogue.text: We’re cutting the trunk into sections. I’ll call when it’s clear.

comic.title: The Open Path
comic.caption: Later that morning, Jonas finishes moving the cut pine onto the moss beside the path. The last section rests with the others; only pale sawdust remains on the tread. He pauses beside the fresh stump and looks along the route that had stopped Mantas earlier. There is room to pass freely now. Jonas takes out his phone and keeps the promise he made during their call. The tractor recovery had got the timber moving; clearing the footpath finishes the job for the people who use the forest on foot.

dialogue.speaker: Jonas
dialogue.text: The path is clear now, Mantas. All the sections are off the trail.

comic.title: A Promise Kept
comic.caption: At the meeting-room doorway, Mantas pauses with his vest over one arm. Jonas’s promised call has arrived: the pine sections are off the tread, and the familiar footpath is open again. Mantas listens, then thanks him for following through. Across the table, Rūta gathers the notes beside the closed laptop. The signup repair has passed its live check; the obstruction that interrupted the run has been cleared too. Neither task needs another urgent decision. Mantas lowers his shoulders. He can change out of his running clothes, then join Rūta for lunch.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Thanks for calling, Jonas. I’m glad the path is clear.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: Lunch after you change?

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Yes. I’ll meet you downstairs.

comic.title: Time to Look Around
comic.caption: By noon, Mantas had changed upstairs and found Rūta at the café below the office. The soup was hot, and for the first time that morning neither of them had a screen between them. Rūta asked about the delay on his run. He described the stuck tractor, the patient tow and Jonas’s call after clearing the path. Beyond the window, the autumn trees caught her attention. She had lived in Vilnius for years without learning many of its forest paths. They agreed on a weekend walk along his familiar loop, with time to look around instead of watching the pace.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: Will you show me that trail this weekend?

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Of course. We can walk the short loop.

comic.title: Room to Walk
comic.caption: That weekend, Mantas and Rūta set out on the short forest loop they had discussed over lunch. A few minutes into the walk, he stopped beside the pale stump. The pine sections lay on the moss, well clear of the tread, just as Jonas had promised. Rūta looked from the cut wood to the open path. Here, the morning’s interruption was already becoming an ordinary part of the landscape. Mantas had passed this place at running pace many times. With someone beside him, there was time to notice it. They would take the rest of the loop slowly.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: This is where the pine blocked the path.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: Now there’s room for both of us.

comic.title: A Different Pace
comic.caption: A few minutes beyond the cleared pine, they take the familiar left-hand return branch. Rūta stops beside a birch and lifts a hand. A woodpecker clings to the pale trunk, tapping in short bursts. Mantas looks up. He has passed this stretch often enough to know every turn, yet cannot remember watching a bird here. They stay still until the tapping resumes. The loop is the same one he runs; at walking pace, with someone else's attention to follow, it has more in it than the route on his watch.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: Listen. Up there.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: I usually run straight past.

comic.title: At Walking Pace
comic.caption: After their pause by the birch, they carry on. The familiar return path takes them through the pines and back to the woodland edge, with no reason to hurry. About half an hour later, they reach the small trailhead clearing together. Mantas gestures back toward the woods. On his weekday run, this had been a place to finish, drink and check the time. Today the same loop has held a cleared passage, a bird he would have missed, and an easy conversation. Rūta smiles beside him as they share the thought.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Same loop. A different morning.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: We had time to notice it.

comic.title: Passing It On
comic.caption: As they turn to leave the clearing, a woman arriving with a walking pole asks whether there is a short route from here. Mantas points along the open path and explains where the familiar left branch brings her back to the trailhead. For once, his directions include room to linger. Rūta smiles and adds that the loop need not take the same amount of time for everyone. The woman listens, looking from his hand to the trees. Their own walk is finished; its discoveries have become something they can pass on.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Take the left branch at the fork. It brings you back here.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: Leave yourself a little time to stop.

dialogue.speaker: Walker
dialogue.text: That sounds just right. Thank you.

comic.title: A Pace to Keep
comic.caption: The woman turned toward the trees and set off with her pole. Mantas and Rūta followed the path toward the exit, leaving the bench and the forest loop behind them. Their morning had ended without a hurry. Rūta suggested trying the same small pause during a workday: a short walk at lunch, with enough time to notice where they were. Mantas agreed. They did not choose a route or a day yet. For now, they kept walking together through the fallen leaves.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: Shall we try a short walk at lunch next week?

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Yes. Let’s make time for it.

comic.title: Ten Minutes Outside
comic.caption: At noon the following Monday, Rūta met Mantas by the office door. They chose a ten-minute loop through the small public garden nearby, leaving enough of their break for lunch afterward. At the garden entrance, Mantas slipped his phone into his pocket. Rūta opened a hand as she suggested a circuit through the autumn trees. The forest was farther away today, but the slower pace was close at hand: a few fallen leaves, a bench in the sun, and a path they could follow without hurrying. They began the loop together.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: Around the garden and back?

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Yes. We have ten minutes.

comic.title: Room for a Small Walk
comic.caption: The garden gate came back into view as their ten-minute circuit ended. On the last curve, Mantas glanced at his watch. His phone had stayed in his pocket throughout the walk, and there was still time for lunch before the afternoon began. Rūta smiled beside him. The streets were only a few steps away. A long run required planning; this little circuit had fitted into the space they already had.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Ten minutes. We have time for lunch.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: Let’s go.

comic.title: Room for a Break
comic.caption: A few minutes after leaving the garden, they found a window table in the nearby café. Their soup was warm, and the office was still within an easy walk. Mantas left his phone in his pocket. The ten-minute circuit had asked for no rearrangement of the day; it had simply given them something else to look at before lunch. Rūta set her scarf over the back of her chair. They could fit another short walk into Wednesday’s break, they agreed, and still leave time to eat.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: Same ten minutes on Wednesday?

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Yes. Let’s keep the time for lunch, too.

comic.title: The Office Door
comic.caption: They finish their soup and walk the few minutes back to the office. At the entrance, Mantas holds the door while Rūta steps into the lobby. The garden loop and lunch have fitted comfortably into their break; there is no need to hurry through the doorway. He has left his phone in his pocket all the way back. The afternoon’s work is waiting upstairs, and Wednesday’s walk is already something they can look forward to.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: Wednesday, same time?

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Same time.

comic.title: One Thing First
comic.caption: Upstairs, their coats went onto hooks and lunch gave way to a table covered in the afternoon’s work. Darius had laid out three improvements for the next release. Mantas put his finger on the nearest card: a clearer explanation of what a new user should do after signing up. The other two could wait until this one had been tested. Rūta opened her notebook and wrote down the task. Their break had ended; the afternoon now had a starting point.

dialogue.speaker: Darius
dialogue.text: Which one goes first?

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: The next step after signup. Let’s make it clear.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: I’ll bring the customer questions.

comic.title: A Clear First Step
comic.caption: Rūta returned with the recent customer questions and set them beside the laptop. The same uncertainty appeared more than once: had signup worked, and where should a new user begin? Mantas opened his notebook and sketched a plain confirmation followed by one clear next action. Darius leaned closer. They would also make it clear that a user could return later. The outline was small enough to try with someone unfamiliar with the product before anyone built it. The two other improvements stayed at the edge of the table.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: They’re asking whether they’re finished—or whether they’ve missed a step.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Confirm the account first. Then show one useful next action.

dialogue.speaker: Darius
dialogue.text: Let’s see if someone new understands the sketch.

comic.title: The First Read
comic.caption: Before anyone turned the sketch into code, Rūta invited Lina from accounts to the table. Lina had never used the signup flow. Mantas set the page in front of her and let her examine it. The confirmation made sense immediately: her account was ready. The large button was less clear. In their draft notes, its proposed label was simply “Continue,” and Lina could not tell whether it opened the account or began another signup step. Rūta wrote down the question. A few quiet minutes had found something the three of them had overlooked.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.text: My account is ready. Does “Continue” open it, or is there another signup step?

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Let’s name where it takes you.

comic.title: A Named Destination
comic.caption: Mantas has replaced the vague action with Open your account. The revised draft lies in front of Lina, and this time she explains the destination without asking another question. Rūta writes down her answer while Darius watches the exchange. The new words have cleared up Lina’s uncertainty about another signup step. That settles one question about the paper draft, but a paper button cannot show whether the route works. Before building the finished guidance, the team will need a clickable prototype that also checks the quieter option to return later.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: What would you expect this action to do?

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.text: My account is ready. This opens it.

comic.title: A Working Route
comic.caption: Half an hour later, the paper draft had become a small clickable prototype. Mantas and Darius had linked the confirmation to a mock account overview. Lina used the main action without coaching. When the overview appeared, she paused, then recognized where she had arrived. Rūta recorded the route and Lina’s explanation beside the earlier wording note. The first destination made sense. They still needed to see whether someone choosing to leave could return without wondering what had happened to the account. The guidance was still a prototype; nothing new had been released.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.text: This is my account. I can start here.

dialogue.speaker: Darius
dialogue.text: Let’s check returning later next.

comic.title: The Way Back
comic.caption: Darius reset the mockup to its confirmation. This time Lina chose the option to return later. It led to a simple signed-out starting page. With no instructions from the others, she found the sign-in route and followed it back to the same mock account overview. Rūta wrote down the sequence while Mantas listened. Leaving had not become a dead end, and returning did not ask Lina to create another account. It was only one colleague’s informal trial, but both routes now made sense to her. The next work was concrete: implement the guidance, then repeat these checks in the product.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.text: I’d sign in here when I’m ready.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: And you found the same account.

comic.title: From Draft to Product
comic.caption: Lina returned to accounts. At the same table, Mantas replaced the mockup with the product running locally and connected the new confirmation. Darius checked how its two choices were wired: opening the account immediately, or leaving and coming back through sign-in. Rūta kept her trial notes beside the laptop, ready to repeat the signup and navigation checks. The implementation was in place, but its behavior still needed testing. Before the guidance could go live, they had to make sure both choices led to the right place and existing details survived the journey.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Both routes are in. Let’s start with a fresh signup.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: Then back and forward, on both routes.

comic.title: Both Ways Back
comic.caption: Darius took the laptop and began with a fresh signup. The new confirmation led him into the account. Then he left, signed in again, and reached the same overview. He repeated the back-and-forward checks while Rūta worked through her notes, comparing each result with the expected behavior. The last check passed. Mantas stood beside him, watching the returned account screen. The guidance now worked in the local product, including the route for someone who chose to return later. Releasing it and checking a fresh live signup were still ahead; the two other improvements could wait.

dialogue.speaker: Darius
dialogue.text: Same account. Both ways.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: I have the steps for the live check.

comic.title: Into the Live Flow
comic.caption: With Darius’s checks recorded, Mantas returned to the keyboard and released the guidance. When the release finished, he passed the laptop to Rūta. She opened a fresh live signup, starting again without the earlier test session. Her notebook held the completed local checks and space beneath them for the live results. The clearer confirmation was now available to customers; the two other improvements remained deferred. Rūta settled her hand on the trackpad. First she would check signup and the main action. Then she would leave and return through sign-in.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: It’s live. Start with a fresh signup.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: Then I’ll check the way back in.

comic.title: Both Ways In
comic.caption: Rūta follows the released flow from a fresh signup. The confirmation makes it clear that the account is ready, and the main action takes her into its overview. She signs out, comes back through sign-in, and reaches the same place. Only then does she mark the last check. Mantas lets his shoulders settle; Darius looks over the recorded results. The guidance they chose after lunch now works in the live product as well as in their local tests. The two other improvements remain on the list, still deferred.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: Both ways bring me back to the account.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Good. That finishes this one.

comic.title: Ten Minutes Kept
comic.caption: By Wednesday lunchtime, the garden path was scattered with yellow leaves. Mantas and Rūta had put on their jackets and come out for the walk they had promised over Monday’s soup. The released guidance task was finished; the two postponed improvements were still waiting at the office. A few steps into the loop, Rūta admitted that she had nearly stayed at her desk. Mantas listened, his phone still in his pocket. They had given themselves ten minutes. For now, they let those minutes belong to the walk.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: I nearly stayed at my desk.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: The list can wait ten minutes.

comic.title: Room for Ten Minutes
comic.caption: The path curved back to the garden gate. Mantas checked his watch: their ten minutes were up, and there was still time for lunch. Rūta gathered the ends of her scarf beside him. The work waiting upstairs had not disappeared, but the walk had given her a little distance from it. They agreed to come out again the following Wednesday. Mantas left his phone in his pocket; the calendar could wait until after lunch.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: Same time next Wednesday?

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Let’s keep the ten minutes.

comic.title: A Decision for Tomorrow
comic.caption: A few minutes beyond the garden gate, they settled beside the café window with bowls of soup. Rūta brought up the two improvements they had left waiting on Monday. Neither needed to be squeezed into the remainder of the break. They agreed to look at recent customer examples together the next morning, then decide which problem deserved their attention first. For now the bowls were warm, the street outside was bright with fallen leaves, and there was still time to eat before returning to the office. Next Wednesday’s walk stayed in their plans.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: Shall we look at the other two tomorrow?

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Bring the customer examples. Then we can choose.

comic.title: The Repeated Question
comic.caption: They finished Wednesday’s lunch and returned to work within their break. On Thursday morning, Rūta brought the customer examples they had promised to review. Three described the same difficulty: once an account held several saved entries, finding an earlier one meant opening them in turn. A fourth asked for an exported overview. Mantas paused over his notebook. The two deferred ideas now had a clearer order. They would sketch a simple search and see whether someone could use it to find a saved entry. Export could wait; the search still had to earn its place.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: These three are trying to find something they already saved.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Let’s test a search before we build it.

comic.title: A Familiar Name
comic.caption: Mantas drew a search field above a short list of saved entries. Rūta made paper results from fictional examples, and Lina came over from accounts for a quick trial. Asked to find one entry, she used the part of its name she remembered. Rūta slid the matching cards beneath the field; Lina selected the right one without another hint. It was a useful first result, though only one attempt. Mantas marked the sketch, then set aside an entry whose name would return no matches. They needed to see what happened when search could not immediately help.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.text: I remember this part of the name.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Now let’s try one that doesn’t match.

comic.title: The Empty Space
comic.caption: For the second trial, Lina tried a name that matched none of the fictional entries. Rūta moved the result cards aside. The space beneath the search field was empty. Lina pointed at it, then looked up. Mantas let the pause stand long enough to hear what she expected. The missing explanation mattered: no matches could look like missing data. They clarified that the entries were still there, and Mantas recorded the question in his notebook. Before building search, they would add a plain explanation and a way to try again, then test the paper version once more.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.text: Does that mean the entry is gone?

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: It is still there. This search found no matches.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: The page should help you try again.

comic.title: A Way Back
comic.caption: Rūta laid a narrow explanation over the empty result area: no entries matched this search, but the saved entries were still there. Beside it, Mantas added one action: Clear search. They offered Lina the revised paper version and waited. She chose the action; Rūta returned the fictional result cards. This time Lina could explain both what had happened and how to recover. Mantas wrote down the result. One person and one small set of cards could not answer every question, but the next decision now had something firmer behind it. Search was still only paper.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.text: Nothing’s gone. I can clear this and start again.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: That’s the recovery we needed to see.

comic.title: A Small Search
comic.caption: With the cards restored, they lay out the three paper states together: a full list, a match, and no match. Lina holds the gathered cards while Rūta points across the sheets and Mantas records the decision. The first version will search saved-entry names within the current account, accepting a name fragment regardless of case or surrounding spaces. They list the checks beside it: find a match, explain no match, then clear the search and recover the full list without changing any saved entry. One colleague’s successful paper trial gives them a direction, not certainty. The next step is a local implementation; export stays deferred.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Name search first. We can build this small version.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: And check all three states before release.

comic.title: The Local Version
comic.caption: A little later that morning, Lina returned to accounts and Mantas opened his laptop. He built the narrow search they had agreed: names in the current account, with case and surrounding spaces ignored. Rūta kept the original fictional cards beside the checklist. In his own local checks, a differently capitalized fragment still found the same entry. A name with no match brought the explanation; clearing the search restored the full list. The saved entries stayed unchanged. These were Mantas’s checks of his own work. The next step was for Darius to repeat them independently before anyone released the change.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: The local version passes my checks. Darius still needs to repeat them.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: I’ll keep the original list with the checklist.

comic.title: A Second Pair of Eyes
comic.caption: Darius pulled a chair to the table and took over the laptop. Mantas let the recorded steps do the explaining. A changed letter case and spaces around the name fragment found the same entry. An absent name brought the explanation that the saved entries were still there. Then Darius cleared the search. The full list returned, and Rūta compared it with the original cards, recording each result. Nothing had disappeared or changed. These were independent local checks, and they had passed. Mantas closed his own notes; the team could now consider releasing search, with a fresh check on the live account still to follow.

dialogue.speaker: Darius
dialogue.text: The list returns unchanged.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: All the recorded checks passed.

comic.title: The Live Check
comic.caption: Mantas released the search after Darius’s independent checks passed. Rūta opened a fresh live session and repeated the same small set of checks: a name fragment with different capitals and surrounding spaces, a search with no matches, then clearing the search. The explanation kept the empty result from implying that an entry had disappeared. When she cleared the field, the full original list returned. Darius watched while she compared it with the baseline. They recorded the successful live check. Search was now available within each account; the saved entries themselves had not changed. Export could wait for its own decision.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: It’s live. Let’s repeat the checks.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: The full list is back. Everything is still here.

comic.title: Closing the Loop
comic.caption: The full list was back where it belonged. Rūta recorded the release and the live checks while Darius gathered the fictional cards into their folder. The paper exercise had done its job; now the account itself could help someone find a remembered name and recover from an empty search. Mantas eased away from the table. They had finished the change they chose, with the saved entries intact. The export request stayed on the later list as the three colleagues returned to the rest of their Thursday work.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: Recorded. All three checks passed.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Good. We can leave this one complete.

comic.title: Room for the Morning
comic.caption: By late Thursday afternoon, ordinary work has filled the hours after the release. Mantas closes his laptop and lifts his jacket from the chair. The completed search can stay completed; export can wait for its turn. At the window, the autumn trees catch the last warm light. He thinks of the familiar forest loop and the time he usually measures against it. Tomorrow, he decides, he will leave early enough to notice more than his pace. Rūta pauses beside him before they head out. Their Wednesday garden walk is still in the diary.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: I’m taking the forest loop tomorrow morning. With time to enjoy it.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: That sounds like a good start.

comic.title: Room for the Morning
comic.caption: Friday morning, Mantas returned to the familiar trail. He had changed into his running kit and left enough time for the loop. At the pine site, the cut sections still lay clear of the path. There was nothing to climb over now. He kept an easy pace, letting the first few minutes settle into a rhythm. Cool air moved through the birches; pale leaves edged the track. Yesterday’s work was finished. For the moment, the next thing to do was simply follow the path into the trees.

comic.title: Time for the Long Way
comic.caption: At the familiar fork, Mantas shortened his stride long enough to choose. The left branch offered the quick return he had taken after the forestry delay and later walked with Rūta. This morning he had left room for the rest of the loop. He turned onto the continuing trail, keeping the same easy pace as the path began to rise between the pines. His phone stayed in his pocket. The week’s search change was finished and checked; nothing needed solving before the next bend. For now, he could give the woods the time he had promised them.

comic.title: Room to Cross
comic.caption: Beyond the rise, the longer trail bends into a shallow hollow. Mantas notices movement between the birches and eases to a stop on firm ground. A roe doe is crossing ahead. He keeps his hands quiet and leaves the space between them open. For a few breaths, the run becomes simply standing still: leaves shifting overhead, the deer placing each hoof, the path continuing beyond it. There is no need to hurry the animal. Once it has moved clear, he can carry on at the same easy pace.

comic.title: The Full Loop
comic.caption: Once the doe disappeared among the saplings, Mantas started again. The first few steps were quiet and short; soon his breathing settled into the familiar rhythm of the longer loop. He followed its bends without trying to recover the minute he had spent waiting. At the woodland edge, the path opened into the modest trailhead clearing. He eased into a walk, the full loop behind him and both flasks still in his vest. There was time for water and a slow cool-down before the rest of Friday began.

comic.title: A Measured Sip
comic.caption: At the edge of the trees, Mantas lets his breathing settle before taking a drink. The longer loop is finished; there is no reason to hurry the last few minutes. He draws one flask from his vest and takes a measured sip, standing quietly beside the leaf-strewn path. The other flask stays in its pocket, and his phone remains put away. Behind him, the familiar trail disappears between birches and pines. He will stow the water again before walking on from the trailhead.

comic.title: The Way Out
comic.caption: Mantas settled the flask back into its pocket and checked that it sat securely beside the other one. Then he walked toward the trailhead exit, letting his breathing ease with each step. Behind him, the narrow forest path disappeared between the birches; ahead, the ground widened into gravel. The longer loop was finished. There was no reason to hurry through these last few metres. With both hands free and his phone still pocketed, he left the woods at a walk.

comic.title: The Bus Home
comic.caption: The broader path brought Mantas to the street beyond the trees. He stopped beside the bus shelter, still feeling the warmth of the run as the morning air cooled his sleeves. Home was a short bus ride away; there was time for a shower and breakfast before work. When the bus appeared, he moved a step back from the curb and waited for it to stop. Both flasks stayed in his vest, and his phone stayed pocketed. The longer loop was finished. The next part of Friday began here.

comic.title: A Seat Toward Home
comic.caption: The bus stopped beside the shelter, and Mantas stepped aboard. A window seat let him rest his legs while the forest edge gave way to the morning street. Both flasks stayed in his vest; his phone stayed in his pocket. He watched the yellow birches pass without reaching for anything. The longer loop was finished, and there was no reason to turn the journey home into another task. First a shower, then breakfast. Work would have its own beginning after that.

comic.title: Back at the Door
comic.caption: At his stop, Mantas left the bus and walked the last few streets home. The run was finished; there was no reason to hurry the rest of the morning. He turned his key, opened the apartment door and stepped onto the mat, bringing a little of the cool outside air with him. His shoes and vest could come off here. Then a shower, breakfast, and the journey to the office. For now, he paused at the threshold before closing the door behind him.

comic.title: Breakfast Before Work
comic.caption: A little later, the running kit was put away and the shower had washed away the last trace of the trail. Mantas settled at his kitchen table in clean clothes, with oats, apple slices and a cup of tea. The morning light reached across the floor toward the orange shoes by the door. He had finished the longer loop, given the deer room to cross, and made his way home without rushing. Now there was time to eat before leaving for work. The forest could remain a forest for a while; the day ahead did not need to begin at the breakfast table.

comic.title: Out the Door
comic.caption: Mantas finishes the last spoonful and carries his bowl and mug to the sink. The kitchen falls quiet again. At the door, he gathers his jacket and settles his work bag on his shoulder; the running vest and orange shoes stay where he put them. A different stretch of the day is waiting now. He opens the door into the shared hallway, leaving himself enough time to reach the office without hurrying.

comic.title: At the Landing
comic.caption: The bus carried Mantas back into the working morning. From his stop, the final block was a short walk; by the time he reached the office stairs, his jacket was open and his phone was still in his pocket. Rūta greeted him at the open doorway. Yesterday's search checks were complete, and the fictional cards had been put away. Before filling the day with another task, she suggested looking over what the week had settled. Mantas held the strap of his bag and agreed to ten minutes. For now, that was enough to begin.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: Shall we review the week before we start anything new?

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Ten minutes. Then we can decide.

comic.title: Ten Minutes to Take Stock
comic.caption: Mantas draped his jacket over the chair and set his work bag beside it. Rūta opened the completed check records. In ten minutes they followed the week's changes from carried-forward details to clear account entry, then to finding and restoring the saved entries. The software checks had passed; Lina's paper search trial still showed only what one person had understood. Mantas rested a finger beside the three small boxes on the sheet. They agreed to begin next week with fresh customer questions before choosing another change. Export stayed on the deferred list. The review ended with a next step small enough to carry out.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: The checks passed. Lina's search trial is still one paper trial.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Let's start next week with the questions people bring us.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: Then choose the next change.

comic.title: The Words They Use
comic.caption: A few minutes later, they stopped at Lina’s desk. Rūta indicated the open notebook, and Lina turned from her accounts work to listen. They would begin collecting fresh questions on Monday: the words people actually used, together with the step where they became uncertain. That would give the team something concrete to compare before choosing another change. Lina agreed to help. The completed checks could stay completed; there was room now for listening. Export remained deferred.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: Keep the question as it was asked.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.text: And the step where they stopped. I can do that.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Then we can decide what deserves work.

comic.title: The First Fresh Question
comic.caption: Monday morning brought the first fresh question. A customer had opened an existing entry and hesitated over its name: would changing it disturb the other details already saved? Lina kept the customer's words, then identified the step where the uncertainty began—before making an edit. Beside her, Rūta recorded both in the notebook. They now had something specific to investigate, but they had not demonstrated a fault. Before giving an answer or choosing another change, they would repeat the steps on a test entry and watch what happened.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.text: They asked, “If I change the name, will the other details stay?”

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: Let’s check a test entry before we answer.

comic.title: The Same Details
comic.caption: They choose a fictional entry, away from customer records. Before touching its name, Lina reads its other saved details while Rūta records a comparison. Lina changes only the name, saves, closes the entry and opens it again. The new name is there; the details they recorded are unchanged. Rūta marks what they actually observed: one test entry, one sequence. It gives them a concrete answer to start from, without turning a customer's uncertainty into a defect or a single check into a promise about every case.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.text: The name changed. These details stayed the same.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: We'll answer with the steps we checked.

comic.title: What We Can Say
comic.caption: Lina turned the comparison into a draft answer. It described the sequence they had actually observed: change the name, save, close, reopen. The other details they had checked were still there. Rūta kept the notebook open beside the draft, making sure it promised no more than that. They added a question about which saved details had worried the customer and where the uncertainty began. The answer was ready to review before sending. A concern had become a clear account of one check and a useful next question; it had not become evidence of a fault.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: We can say what we checked.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.text: And ask which details worried them.

comic.title: A Careful Answer
comic.caption: Rūta called Mantas across from his nearby desk. He read Lina's draft, then compared it with the recorded sequence in the notebook: one fictional entry, only its name changed, saved, closed and reopened. The other details they had checked were still there. The answer could say that much. It could not settle a concern the customer had not yet described. After the brief review, Lina sent the reply, including their two questions: which details worried the customer, and at what step had the uncertainty begun? There was no new defect to assign. They would keep the customer's exact answer when it arrived.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Keep it to what we checked. The questions stay.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.text: Sent. I'll add their reply to the notes.

comic.title: Before Save
comic.caption: Twenty minutes later, the answer arrived. The customer was worried about the saved email address and telephone number, and the uncertainty began just before pressing Save after changing the name. Lina turned from her laptop and read the question aloud. Rūta wrote the wording and the step into her notebook while Mantas drew a chair alongside the desk. Their earlier check still described only one fictional example. Now they had a specific concern to compare with the actual edit screen before deciding what, if anything, needed to change.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.text: The email and telephone details. They hesitate just before Save.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Let’s look at that moment on the screen.

comic.title: Before Save
comic.caption: Lina opens the edit screen for a fictional entry. The name, email and telephone fields sit together above one Save action. Rūta compares that view with the customer’s exact question; Mantas points to the place where the customer had hesitated. The screen offers no review of which fields have changed. Their earlier check still stands: the other details they checked survived a name-only edit. This concern does not establish a defect. They agree to sketch a small review of changed fields above Save, using made-up details, then check whether it makes the scope clear before writing code. The draft’s usefulness remains an open question.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.text: Here—all three fields lead to the same Save.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Let’s make the changed fields visible in a draft.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: Then check whether that answers this question.

comic.title: What Stays the Same
comic.caption: Mantas copied their fictional entry onto paper and placed a before-and-after name row above the sketched Save button. Lina traced the two contact rows with her finger. A list of changes might still leave her original worry unanswered: what would happen to the details left out of it? Mantas added an explicit indication that the email and telephone would remain unchanged. Rūta recorded the addition beside the customer’s exact concern. They now had a draft that addressed both the change and the details to be kept. Its clarity still needed a separate test before anyone wrote code.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.text: If only the name is listed, do these two stay the same?

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Let’s make that explicit in the draft.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: Then we can check whether people understand it.

comic.title: An Unaided Read
comic.caption: They turn the revised sheet toward Darius, who has not helped draw it. Rūta asks what he expects to happen when he saves; Mantas leaves the pencil down and waits. Darius follows the name change, then indicates the two contact rows. He expects the email and telephone to remain as they are. Rūta records his answer before the discussion resumes. One unaided colleague read supports the draft's clarity, though it says nothing yet about customer use. They agree to build a local prototype and check that saving the new name preserves the unchanged contacts.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: Before you save, what will change?

dialogue.speaker: Darius
dialogue.text: Only the name. Email and telephone stay the same.

comic.title: The First Local Check
comic.caption: Twenty minutes later, the paper review has become a local prototype on Mantas’s laptop. He changes the name of a fictional entry, reviews the change, saves it, then closes and reopens the entry. The new name is there; the email address and telephone number still match the starting sample. Rūta records the sequence and its result. It is one check on his own work, enough to hand the prototype over for an independent attempt. Darius takes the original sample sheet so he can compare for himself. Their customers’ accounts remain untouched.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: The contacts survived my check. Try it from the start.

dialogue.speaker: Darius
dialogue.text: I’ll compare the reopened entry with the original.

comic.title: The Same Details
comic.caption: Darius takes the laptop and begins again from the original fictional sample. Mantas steps back, leaving him to follow the review without prompts. Darius changes the name, compares the proposed change with the baseline, saves, closes the record and opens it again. The new name is there. He checks the email and telephone against the sheet beside the laptop; both are unchanged. Rūta records the sequence and the independent result. Their two local checks now agree. The question that began at the shared Save button has a clearer answer in the prototype, but the release decision still lies ahead.

dialogue.speaker: Darius
dialogue.text: The name changed. Both contact details stayed.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: We have the independent result. Now we can decide on release.

comic.title: The Live Check
comic.caption: With both local checks recorded, Mantas released the name-review guidance. Rūta began again on the live service, using a dedicated fictional test account and fresh starting details. Before saving, she compared the proposed name with the original and checked the email and telephone shown as unchanged. Then she saved, closed the account and reopened it. The new name was still there; both contact details matched their starting values. Darius watched beside the table while Mantas kept his hands away from the keyboard. Rūta recorded the result. The question before Save now had a visible answer, supported by a completed live check.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: The name stayed. Email and telephone match.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Record the live result. That completes this change.

comic.title: A Precise Reply
comic.caption: With Rūta’s live check recorded, Mantas joins her at Lina’s desk. Lina writes a short follow-up: the new review shows the name before and after the change, alongside the email and telephone details that will remain unchanged. She invites the customer to open that review and check it before deciding whether to save. Rūta keeps the test record beside her; it supports their explanation, but it cannot tell them what the customer will understand. Lina sends the reply and leaves the conversation open. They have answered the specific worry without changing the customer’s account or treating uncertainty as a defect.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.text: I’ll ask them to look at the review before they save.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: And tell us what is still unclear.

comic.title: The Reply
comic.caption: The answer arrived later that morning, while the three were still at Lina’s desk. She turned from the screen and read it aloud. Rūta copied the wording into her notebook and marked it as one customer’s report: the name had been saved and reopened, and the contact details were unchanged. The team had not opened or changed that account themselves. Mantas let his shoulders relax. The question that had started this work finally had a specific answer. They could close this particular follow-up and leave export for another day.

dialogue.speaker: Lina, reading the customer’s reply
dialogue.text: I checked the review, saved the name, and reopened it. My email and telephone are still the same.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Record those words. We can close this question.

comic.title: The Wet Pavement
comic.caption: By the end of Monday, the office had returned to its ordinary rhythm. Mantas finished his afternoon work, pulled on his olive jacket and walked to the nearby bus stop. Rain tapped the shelter roof and darkened the fallen leaves along the curb. He watched the water gather between them while he waited to go home. Tomorrow, he decided, he would look at the forest ground in daylight before choosing the length of his run. The weather outside the office could suggest caution; it could not tell him what lay on the trail.

comic.title: Homeward
comic.caption: The bus arrived before the rain eased. Mantas found a seat by the window and settled his work bag against his knees. Warm light caught the droplets on the glass; outside, street lamps stretched into amber streaks across the wet pavement. His phone stayed in his pocket. For the rest of the ride, there was nothing he needed to settle. Tomorrow’s distance could wait until he had seen the forest ground in daylight. Tonight, the bus would take him home.

comic.title: Across the Threshold
comic.caption: By the time Mantas reaches his stop, the last daylight has gone. He walks the remaining streets and lets himself into his apartment, carrying the damp smell of the evening into the warm hall. He lowers his work bag beside the door and reaches back to close it. Tomorrow’s distance can wait until he sees the trail in daylight. Tonight he needs to eat, dry his jacket and rest. The customer’s answer is settled for now; there is no reason to turn the quiet evening into another work session.

comic.title: A Quiet Supper
comic.caption: After hanging his jacket, Mantas warmed a bowl of vegetable soup and brought bread to the small kitchen table. The apartment settled into its familiar evening sounds: the low hum of the refrigerator, rain against the glass, a spoon touching the bowl. He ate slowly, letting the day loosen its grip. Tomorrow’s route could wait until he saw the forest in daylight. For tonight, there was nothing more to decide. He would wash the few dishes, get his running kit ready, and go to bed at his usual time.

comic.title: The Last Bowl
comic.caption: After the soup, Mantas carries the few dishes to the sink. Warm water clears the bowl, plate, glass and spoon; the table is empty again. He dries the bowl while the city lights soften behind the rain on the window. His phone stays in his pocket. There is no reason to choose a distance tonight: the forest ground still needs a look in daylight. For now, he has finished dinner and nearly finished the washing up. Once the bowl is put away, he can hang the towel and get ready for bed.

comic.title: Lights Out
comic.caption: Mantas puts the dry bowl in the cupboard and leaves the kitchen ready for breakfast. In the bedroom, he changes into soft sleep clothes and sets his phone face-down to charge. The rain is still visible against the dark city window. He sits on the edge of the bed and reaches for the lamp. Tomorrow, daylight will let him check the forest ground before deciding how far to run. There is no need to choose from here. For now, the day is finished.

comic.title: A Shorter Morning
comic.caption: By Tuesday daylight, the night’s rain had become a question he could answer with his feet. After sleep, breakfast and the journey to the woodland edge, Mantas stopped before starting his watch. A shallow puddle held the pale sky; wet leaves lay across the exposed roots. He set one shoe carefully at the edge and tested his footing. This first stretch was enough to make the longer run less appealing, though it told him nothing certain about the ground farther in. He chose the familiar short loop at an easy pace, ready to slow to a walk wherever the footing required it.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: The short loop today. Easy from the start.

comic.title: An Easy Start
comic.caption: Beyond the first puddle, Mantas begins with short, unhurried strides. Rain has darkened the earth, but a narrow strip of firm ground still shows through the fallen leaves. He follows that visible line, looking a few steps ahead instead of trying to recover the pace of a dry morning. The trailhead drops out of view as the path bends among the birches and pines. He is moving comfortably now; that is enough for the opening minutes. The ground around the next curve will need its own look. For the moment, the familiar short loop gives him room to settle into the run.

comic.title: The Narrow Strip
comic.caption: Around the bend, the trail dipped and the rain had collected across its middle. Mantas shortened his stride, then let the jog become a walk. A strip of exposed earth remained along the inner edge, wide enough to use without stepping into the wet leaves beyond the path. He placed one orange shoe on it and looked ahead for the next foothold. The short loop would still be there if he took a few slower steps. For now, keeping his balance mattered more than keeping his pace.

comic.title: Beyond the Dip
comic.caption: The firm strip widens beyond the puddle. Mantas takes the last walking steps onto the rise, checks the earth ahead, and lets his stride lengthen into an easy jog. Behind him the shallow water settles around yellow leaves; ahead, the trail bends between birches and pines. There is no need to make up time. He keeps the pace of a short, wet-morning run, shortening his steps where roots break the surface. He is clear of the dip, alone and uninjured, with the familiar loop still ahead.

comic.title: The Loop Completed
comic.caption: The remaining bends brought Mantas back to the woodland edge. He had kept the same easy effort wherever the ground allowed it, shortening his steps when wet leaves covered the trail. Now the narrow path opened into the familiar clearing, and he slowed to a walk. The short loop was finished. Nothing had required him to hurry. The brief walk past the puddle had simply become part of the run. He let his breathing settle as he crossed the firm ground, still alone, with both flasks in his vest. Before leaving, he would take a drink.

comic.title: A Small Drink
comic.caption: A little walking brings his breathing back to an easy rhythm. Beside the trailhead bench, Mantas draws a flask from his vest and takes a small drink. Damp leaves lie flat on the firm ground; beyond the birches, the city is beginning its morning. The short loop has given him what he wanted today: movement, fresh air and enough time to notice his footing. He lets the pause last another moment before putting the flask away and heading out of the forest.

comic.title: Leaving the Trees
comic.caption: Mantas pressed the flask back into its front pocket and checked that it sat securely. With both hands free, he left the bench behind and followed the firm path toward the woodland edge. The short loop was finished; he could let the rest of the morning begin at a walking pace. Damp leaves shifted beneath his orange shoes, and the city showed through gaps between the trunks. He would head home, put away his running kit and get ready for work.

comic.title: The Homeward Bus
comic.caption: The woodland path brought Mantas to the roadside stop. When the bus arrived, he let it settle against the curb before stepping through the open door. The short loop had fitted into the morning without a rush; now he could carry that pace home. Both flasks stayed in their pockets as he reached for the entrance rail. Outside, damp yellow leaves marked the edge of the pavement. There was still time to put away the running kit, wash and change before returning to work.

comic.title: The Kit by the Door
comic.caption: The bus carried Mantas from the woodland edge back into his neighbourhood. After the short walk from his stop, he let himself into the flat and closed the door behind him. He slipped off the orange trail shoes onto the entry mat and hung the hydration vest on its hook, with both flasks still in their pockets. The morning’s run was finished; there was no need to hurry through the next part. A shower and clean clothes would come before the journey to work.

comic.title: Before the Bus
comic.caption: After a shower, Mantas changed into his clean teal sweater and charcoal trousers. He sat down to a warm bowl of porridge before reaching for his work bag. Outside the window, the wet roofs of Vilnius caught the morning light. The short loop had left him pleasantly tired, with enough time to eat. He left his phone beside the mug and began breakfast. The next journey would be the familiar bus ride to the office.

comic.title: The Morning Bus
comic.caption: Breakfast finished, Mantas rinsed his bowl, pocketed his phone and picked up his work bag. At the familiar stop, the next bus arrived while the pavement shone with rain. Now, seated beside the window, he watched ochre trees and pale façades pass. The short run had left him comfortably awake. There was time to reach the office without hurrying, and no unfinished customer reply waiting from yesterday. For a few stops, he let the city set the pace.

comic.title: A Question at the Door
comic.caption: A few stops later, Mantas left the bus and walked to the office. He climbed the familiar stairs with his work bag, the morning run already behind him. Lina met him at the open doorway with a fresh customer question she had kept in the customer’s own words. This time the uncertainty concerned sharing two particular entries. Mantas paused before setting down his bag. Export had been deferred; one question was a reason to understand the task, not yet a reason to choose a solution.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.text: A new question: “How can I send just two entries to a colleague?”

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Let’s find out what they need to send.

comic.title: Before Choosing a Format
comic.caption: Mantas set his work bag beside Lina's desk. The customer's sentence named two entries and a colleague, but left the purpose open. Lina laid the question beside two fictional paper cards while they worked out what to ask next. Which details needed to travel with each entry? Would the colleague simply read them, or need to keep working with them? Lina drafted a brief clarification. Until an answer came back, they had a question to pursue rather than a feature to build. The earlier follow-up stayed closed, and export stayed deferred.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Which details does the colleague need?

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.text: I'll ask how they plan to use them, too.

comic.title: What the Colleague Needs
comic.caption: Lina sent the questions they had drafted. Later that morning, a reply arrived: the colleague needed only the names and current statuses of the two entries for tomorrow's planning meeting, and would read them rather than edit them. Mantas pulled a chair beside her desk. Lina laid their two blank example cards beside a sheet of paper and recorded the reply. The answer narrowed the request, but they still needed to work out a useful way to share those details. They agreed to sketch a small fictional example next. Export remained deferred, and Monday's completed follow-up stayed closed.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.text: Names and current statuses. Just to read at tomorrow’s meeting.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Let’s sketch it with the two example cards first.

comic.title: The Time of the Snapshot
comic.caption: The two blank cards gave way to a single sheet. Lina sketched two fictional entries, each reduced to a name and its status, then paused over the page. A status could change before Wednesday's meeting. Mantas added a small clock mark above the example: they needed to make clear when this information had been current. The drawing offered a way to discuss a dated snapshot, but it had proved nothing yet. Before choosing a sharing method, they would check whether its reader understood that limit.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.text: When were these statuses current?

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Let's make the time clear in the example.

comic.title: A Date Beside the Clock
comic.caption: Mantas slid the sheet closer to Lina and asked her to read it as the colleague would. These were the two statuses at the marked moment, she said, not a promise about Wednesday. But which day did that moment belong to? A small calendar outline now sat beside the clock, and Lina pointed to it as they discussed the gap. Their next draft needed a plain date and time, with a clear explanation that the statuses could change afterward. This one paper trial had helped. The entries remained fictional, and they still had to choose how to share them.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.text: The statuses are from that moment. But which day?

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Then the snapshot needs a date as well as a time.

comic.title: A Moment, Clearly Marked
comic.caption: Mantas replaces the clock and calendar hints with a plain date and time above the two fictional rows. Beneath them he adds a brief warning: the statuses may change after that moment. Lina lifts the revised sheet and reads it again. This time she describes it as Tuesday's snapshot, something to check afresh before Wednesday's meeting. Her reading gives them a useful result from one small paper trial. They agree to try the same two names and statuses in a copyable message draft, carrying the date, time and warning with them. The laptop remains untouched; nothing has been sent.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.text: I can tell when these statuses were recorded. I would check again before the meeting.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Let’s keep that date and warning with the two rows when we try the message draft.

comic.title: The Date Travels With It
comic.caption: Mantas set the original worksheet face down and handed Lina the message draft. The two fictional names and statuses were unchanged; the same Tuesday date and time headed the note, and its final line warned that statuses could change. Lina read it without the worksheet and explained that her colleague should check again before Wednesday’s meeting. The date had survived the shorter format. Mantas recorded this as one paper check and proposed an independent reading before they chose whether to build anything.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.text: It tells me when these were checked. I’d check them again tomorrow.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Let Rūta read it on its own.

comic.title: A Second Reading
comic.caption: Rūta pulled up a chair and read the draft without an explanation from either of them. The two rows were useful, she said, provided the recipient treated them as a record of Tuesday morning. They could not promise what would still be true at Wednesday’s meeting. Mantas noted the agreement between two limited paper readings. That was enough to keep the wording for this small manual task. Lina would obtain current statuses before composing any real message tomorrow. For now, the fictional draft stayed on paper, and the original worksheet stayed face down.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: These are Tuesday’s statuses. I’d check again before Wednesday.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Then we keep this request manual.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.text: I’ll get the current statuses before I send anything.

comic.title: A Quiet Lunch
comic.caption: With the paper review finished, Mantas and Rūta walked downstairs and into the nearby café. Lina stayed upstairs with responsibility for obtaining fresh statuses before any real Wednesday message. Over two bowls of soup, Mantas started to reach for his notebook, then tucked it back into the black bag beside his chair. The morning already had a stopping point. He turned toward Rūta and the window, where wind carried yellow leaves along the pavement. They would return within their lunch break; Wednesday’s garden walk could wait for Wednesday.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: I keep trying to fill the pause.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: Then let lunch be the next thing.

comic.title: Back at an Easy Pace
comic.caption: After soup, the short walk back gave Mantas no reason to hurry. At the top of the office stairs, he shifted the black bag on his shoulder and let Rūta draw level. His notebook was still closed inside it; his phone stayed in his pocket. They had returned with time left in their lunch break. The afternoon would begin soon enough. For now, the window held a small square of October light, and neither of them needed to fill the remaining minutes with another decision. Tomorrow’s garden walk could keep its place in the day.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: Same time for the garden tomorrow?

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Yes. Let’s keep it.

comic.title: A Place in the Morning
comic.caption: Inside the office, Mantas set his bag beside his desk and opened the notebook. Lina stopped before returning to her own work. The two names were still a manual request, but the next step now had a place in the morning: she would obtain both fresh statuses on Wednesday, then bring the wording back for a quick review before sending anything. Mantas wrote a short reminder. Beside them, Rūta opened her laptop. The afternoon began with tomorrow’s small task assigned, without turning Tuesday’s example into tomorrow’s truth.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.text: I’ll bring the fresh statuses tomorrow morning.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Then we’ll check the wording before it goes.

comic.title: Two Current Lines
comic.caption: The rest of Tuesday passed in ordinary desk work. On Wednesday morning, Lina returned with two status confirmations obtained directly from the people responsible. She laid the notes beside her manual draft. Each name had its own current status line, followed by the time of the recheck. Mantas read the draft against both notes and handed it back. The review was finished. Lina would send the message herself, using these fresh confirmations rather than Tuesday’s fictional worksheet.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.text: Both checked this morning.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Each name has its own current status. This is ready.

comic.title: The Message Goes
comic.caption: Lina sets the reviewed draft beside her laptop, with both source notes within reach. Each name has its own freshly confirmed status; the recheck time and the warning about later changes remain in the message. She gives the wording one final look and sends it herself. Mantas rests his hands beside his closed notebook. The small request has reached its destination without needing a new feature or a visit to anyone's account. Rūta continues her work nearby as the office returns to its quiet Wednesday rhythm. Their ten-minute garden walk still belongs to the coming break.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.text: Sent. The recheck time is there.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Thanks for checking both.

comic.title: Ten Minutes Outside
comic.caption: Wednesday’s morning work settled into its usual rhythm after Lina’s message went out. At their agreed lunch break, Mantas and Rūta went downstairs and made the slow loop through the office garden. The ten-minute walk brought them back beside the entrance, with time left for lunch. A breeze shook a handful of yellow leaves loose; Rūta paused to watch them fall. Mantas kept his phone in his pocket. The message was sent, the walk was done, and soup was next.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: Shall we get soup?

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Yes. We have time.

comic.title: A Table by the Window
comic.caption: The café windows framed the same yellow leaves they had just walked beneath. Mantas and Rūta settled at a small table with soup and bread, letting the warmth replace the garden breeze. For a few minutes, their conversation stayed with the changing trees and the pleasure of getting outside in the middle of an ordinary working day. Their spoons hovered above the bowls. They had time to eat comfortably before returning upstairs, and neither felt a need to hurry the other through the pause.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: Soup, then back upstairs?

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Yes. We still have time.

comic.title: Back Upstairs
comic.caption: With the soup bowls empty, Mantas and Rūta left the café and took the stairs back to the office. They reached the landing before their lunch break ended. Mantas pushed the familiar door open; yellow leaves were still visible through the stairwell window. The walk and lunch had given the morning a clean ending. Lina’s reviewed message had already been sent, and there was nothing to reopen on her behalf. Mantas’s black bag and notebook waited inside. He was ready to pick up the afternoon’s ordinary work.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: That was a useful pause.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: Back with a clear head.

comic.title: A Quiet Review
comic.caption: The office door fell shut behind them, and Mantas returned to the desk where his notebook and black bag had waited through lunch. Rūta settled at her own screen. Before Mantas chose his first task, Darius drew a chair alongside him and turned a laptop so they could both see it. He had a small maintenance change ready for another pair of eyes. Mantas opened his notebook. They would begin with what the change was meant to preserve, then look through it together. The afternoon had found its first clear task.

dialogue.speaker: Darius
dialogue.text: Could you look at this with me before I merge it?

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Of course. What should stay the same?

comic.title: The Extra Call
comic.caption: Darius’s small maintenance change gathered the search input’s cleanup into a shared helper. As they followed its uses, Mantas found one draft call that would also trim the names shown in the overview. That reached beyond the intended job. They agreed to keep cleanup at the search input and preserve saved names exactly as before. Darius removed the extra call while Mantas noted what to check: mixed-case fragments, surrounding spaces, no match, and Clear search. The review had narrowed the scope. The corrected draft still needed local checks; nothing had been merged or released.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Only the search input. The names stay as they are.

dialogue.speaker: Darius
dialogue.text: I’ll remove that call, then we can check the behavior.

comic.title: The Same Names
comic.caption: Darius worked through the four cases in the corrected local draft: a mixed-case fragment, spaces around the query, a search with no match, and Clear search.
