The fictional entries behaved as before. When the full list returned, they compared its names with the untouched examples; the extra cleanup had stayed out of the display path. Mantas put the last tick in his notebook. A small maintenance change could earn its place by leaving familiar behavior intact. The checks were complete, but the draft still needed its final review before any merge or release.

dialogue.speaker: Darius
dialogue.text: Four checks. Same names.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Ready for the final review.

comic.title: The Narrow Change
comic.caption: Mantas turns from the restored entry list to the corrected change itself. The extra call is gone: only the search query is cleaned up, while the saved names keep their original form. Darius points out the narrow change, and Mantas follows the helper into its caller before finishing the review. Then his hand returns to the trackpad and he completes the merge. Their small maintenance task has moved forward without widening its scope. Deployment and a fresh live check are still ahead; for now, the running service continues as it was.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Query input only. Reviewed and merged.

dialogue.speaker: Darius
dialogue.text: Then deployment and the fresh live checks.

comic.title: Names Kept Intact
comic.caption: Mantas deployed the reviewed correction, then gave Rūta the laptop for a fresh live test session with fictional entries. She tried a mixed-case fragment with spaces around it; the expected names appeared. A fragment with no matches left the explanation in place, and Clear search brought the entries back. She compared the displayed names with their originals, including the spacing they had deliberately preserved. Nothing had been trimmed. Darius recorded the completed checks. The small maintenance task was finished, and the three could return to the afternoon’s work. Export remained deferred.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: The search still works. The names are untouched.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Good. We can close this one.

comic.title: Define the Work
comic.caption: With the maintenance recorded as complete, Darius returned to his own desk. Mantas opened the afternoon’s planning draft: a proposed support colleague. The document listed tools, but it said little about what the person would actually own. He drew a fresh outline in his notebook—answer routine questions, record uncertainty, and bring decisions to the responsible person. Rūta paused beside him with the draft. They agreed to make those boundaries clear before recruitment began. The verified search could keep doing its job while they worked out this different kind of responsibility.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Let’s define the work before we advertise it.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: And say where a question goes when they can’t answer it.

comic.title: A Clear Boundary
comic.caption: Mantas turned the broad idea of helping customers into a few concrete duties: record the exact question and the step that caused uncertainty, then answer from guidance the team had already checked. Rūta placed the draft beside his notebook and added a boundary. If the reported behavior was unclear, or the answer depended on a change, the support colleague would bring the details to the responsible teammate and arrange a follow-up. They would promise only what had been confirmed. By the end of the discussion, the role had a practical scope. Recruitment could now be drafted around it.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: The first job is to understand the question.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: And know when to bring it to the team.

comic.title: A Draft Takes Shape
comic.caption: Rūta pulled up a chair and opened a fresh document. The agreed duties became a recruitment draft: listen carefully, write clear replies, use checked guidance and keep track of follow-ups. Mantas added a small exercise using fictional details. An applicant would explain one known step, then identify a question that needed a teammate’s help. They wanted to see careful judgement as well as fluent writing. By the time the afternoon light reached the edge of the desk, they had something concrete for Lina to review. The draft stayed with them; it had not been posted, and nobody had been hired.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: Clear writing, careful listening—and knowing when to ask.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Let’s show that in the exercise.

comic.title: A Promise They Can Keep
comic.caption: Lina joined them at the desk and read the draft alongside the fictional exercise. One sentence stopped her pencil: the new colleague would promise when a question would be resolved. That was more than the support role could know. She suggested arranging the next update with the responsible teammate instead. Rūta revised the sentence, and Mantas added the same distinction to the exercise: explain what is checked, identify what remains uncertain, and agree how the answer will return. Lina approved the revised draft. It was ready for the next practical decision, but still had not been posted.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.text: We can agree on the next update. We cannot promise an answer we do not have.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: I’ll make that clear in the role and the exercise.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Then we should decide who will handle the applications.

comic.title: A Named Next Step
comic.caption: The approved draft still needed an owner on the other side of it. Lina took the folder as they settled the work behind the invitation: she would receive applications and acknowledge them; she and Rūta would read the fictional exercise together before making a shortlist. Mantas would join the interviews that followed. Lina added one last practical note to the plan—check everyone’s availability before offering a time. The responsibilities now had names beside them. Their recruitment notice remained unposted, but they could publish it without leaving incoming applications to chance.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.text: I’ll receive them and acknowledge each one.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: We’ll review the exercise together.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Then I’ll join the interviews.

comic.title: The Notice Goes Live
comic.caption: Lina brought the approved notice up on the office laptop. With the application handling already written down, she checked the contact address against the folder and posted it. Rūta stayed beside her while they opened the public page afresh and checked that the exercise attachment opened as well. The work had moved one step beyond a draft: someone looking for the role could now find it and apply. Mantas let Lina finish the checks before closing the folder. There were no applications yet. For now, Lina had a clear place to receive them, and the three of them knew what would happen next.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.text: It’s live. The address and exercise both check out.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: I’ll review the responses with you when they arrive.

comic.title: The First Reply
comic.caption: Later that afternoon, the recruitment mailbox received its first application. Lina checked the covering note and completed fictional exercise, then wrote a brief acknowledgement of receipt. She promised no interview: the review still had to happen. Rūta pulled up a chair and took the exercise sheet while Mantas returned to his own work. The first question asked how to handle a customer waiting for an answer. Together, Lina and Rūta would compare the response with the same criteria they had approved for the notice. For now, one application had arrived and been acknowledged. No decision had been made.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.text: Received. Now we read it carefully.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: Let’s start with what the customer is actually asking.

comic.title: Reasons Before Names
comic.caption: Lina laid the approved criteria beside the completed exercise. Together she and Rūta traced the response from the customer's exact question to the guidance that had actually been checked. Where the fictional case lacked an answer, the applicant proposed escalation and a follow-up, with an agreed time for the next update rather than a promise of resolution. They recorded their reasons before adding this application to the shortlist. At the other desks, the afternoon's ordinary work continued. An interview would be the next decision, after Lina checked the applicant's and team's availability.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.text: The next update is clear. The outcome stays uncertain.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: Put this one on the shortlist. Next we check everyone’s availability.

comic.title: Before Booking
comic.caption: Lina left the review sheets in their folder and brought her notebook to Mantas's desk. He checked his calendar; Rūta checked hers. They found two possible interview windows, and Lina recorded both before sending the shortlisted applicant a brief request for availability. She asked which window would suit and left room to suggest another. Nothing was booked yet. The applicant's reply would show whether those windows were useful; only then would Lina send an invitation.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: These two windows work for me.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: Mine too.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.text: I'll check before booking.

comic.title: A Place in the Calendar
comic.caption: A little later, the applicant’s reply arrives: the Thursday morning window works. Lina checks that the slot is still free for both Mantas and Rūta, then prepares a calendar invitation with the agreed time, meeting link, and a brief outline: discuss the exercise, then leave space for the applicant’s questions. Rūta checks the details before Lina sends it. The notebook now has one confirmed appointment. The exercise and assessment notes stay together for tomorrow; the selection decision will wait until they have spoken.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.text: Thursday morning works for them.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Let’s leave room for their questions, too.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: The details match. Send it.

comic.title: The Late Check
comic.caption: Thursday morning, the invitation became a conversation. Eglė joined the call at the agreed time, and Mantas asked her to explain the choices in her exercise. Rūta listened beside him while Lina recorded their notes. They then changed one detail in the fictional case: the person responsible had not returned a check by the expected time. Eglė said she would tell the customer what was still unconfirmed, acknowledge the delay, and agree another update time she could keep. She would not turn that update into a promise of resolution. The interview was underway; they still had her questions to hear and evidence to consider.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: If the check is late, what changes in your reply?

dialogue.speaker: Eglė
dialogue.text: I explain the delay and agree the next update. I cannot promise the result.

comic.title: Learning Alongside
comic.caption: The exercise gave way to Eglė’s own question: how would a newcomer learn the work without guessing? Rūta described starting beside Lina—reading real questions, drafting replies from checked guidance, and reviewing them together before anything went out. Where a question exceeded that guidance, they would take it to the colleague responsible for the work. Lina paused her pen to follow the exchange. The conversation now tested both sides: what the applicant could bring, and what the team could teach. This was an approach discussed in an interview, not a job offer. Mantas kept listening.

dialogue.speaker: Eglė
dialogue.text: Who checks my replies while I’m learning?

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: We’d begin alongside Lina, and review the replies together.

comic.title: A Clear Next Step
comic.caption: Eglė welcomed the chance to learn beside Lina. What mattered to her was understanding why a reply changed, so the next draft could be better. With her remaining questions answered, the conversation settled into a quiet thank-you. Lina laid her pen across the notebook. Before ending the call, Mantas gave Eglė a definite time for the next update: Friday at noon. The interview had reached its close. The team still needed to assess what they had heard; the friendly goodbye carried no offer or hiring decision.

dialogue.speaker: Eglė
dialogue.text: I'd like to understand why a draft changes, so I can use that judgement next time.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Thank you, Eglė. We'll send you an update by tomorrow at noon.

comic.title: The Evidence on the Table
comic.caption: Once the call ended, Lina reopened her notebook. They returned to the approved criteria and the examples Eglė had actually given: checked guidance, referral when uncertain, and a next update kept separate from a promised resolution. Rūta set those answers beside the exercise; Mantas listened before agreeing. They would offer Eglė the support role, with Lina reviewing her early drafts and explaining each change. Lina recorded the decision. Eglė did not know it yet. The written offer still needed preparation and checking before the update Mantas had promised by Friday noon.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.text: She knew when to check before answering.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: And she asked to understand the feedback.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Let’s offer her the role, with that support in place.

comic.title: Ready to Send
comic.caption: A few minutes later, the laptop was open again. Mantas set the offer beside the notes they had just agreed, and Lina checked that the responsibilities matched. Rūta read the promise of explained feedback on early drafts, then paused at the proposed start date. They could suggest a day; Eglė still needed to agree to it. The team checked the wording once more and left the offer ready to send. Their decision had become something the applicant could read and consider. For now, Eglė knew only that her next update would arrive by Friday noon.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: Let’s make clear that the start date is a proposal.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.text: And the draft review is here, as we agreed.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Good. This is ready to send.

comic.title: The Offer Goes Out
comic.caption: The checked pages lay beside the laptop. With their decision recorded and the offer checked, Mantas attached the agreed document and sent it to Eglė while Rūta and Lina sat with him. It was still Thursday morning, comfortably ahead of the update he had promised by Friday noon. The proposed start date needed her agreement, and the early-draft support was written plainly. Lina set her pen down. Their part was done for now. Eglė would need time to read, ask questions and decide. Her receipt and response were still unconfirmed.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: The offer’s sent.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.text: We’ll leave room for her questions.

comic.title: Room for a Week
comic.caption: Near midday, a reply brings Eglė back into the room without another call. She has received the offer and asks whether she can begin one week after the proposed date; she needs to finish an existing commitment. Lina opens the team calendar while Rūta checks the planned review sessions. The later week leaves room for those sessions. Mantas replies with the revised date and asks Eglė to confirm it when she decides. The offer is now a conversation, but it is still an offer: she has not accepted the role.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.text: We can keep the review sessions in that week.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Then she can finish her commitment first.

comic.title: A Place on the Calendar
comic.caption: Before lunch, Eglė's reply arrived. She accepted the offer and confirmed the revised start, one week later, giving her time to finish her existing commitment. Mantas read the two confirmations aloud. Lina marked the agreed start in her planner while Rūta leaned closer to check the first review slot. The quiet satisfaction around the table soon became practical work: gather the customer examples they had already checked, and make the first morning easy to follow. Eglė had not started yet. Now the team could prepare for the day she would.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: She has accepted—and confirmed the later start.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: Let's gather the checked examples for her first morning.

comic.title: A Small First Step
comic.caption: A few minutes later, Rūta brought two already checked customer examples into a small first-morning packet. A brief guide lay beside them: record the exact question, use the checked guidance, and flag anything still uncertain. Mantas suggested pausing after the first practice reply. Lina would explain her review before Eglė sent any customer message. They set the materials beside the planner for a final check before the agreed start. Eglė remained remote and had not yet begun work.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: One practice reply, then a review together.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.text: I'll explain what I check, and why.

comic.title: Ready for the First Morning
comic.caption: Lina checked the brief guide against both customer examples, reading the steps aloud while Rūta followed the pages. Each example kept the customer’s exact question, the checked guidance and the point where a reply needed another person’s help. An agreed next update stayed separate from any promise of a resolution. Mantas listened, then nodded. Lina clipped the three sheets together: a small, usable packet for the morning that was still a week away. Eglė had accepted, but she had not started. The preparation was ready; the first practice reply would wait for her arrival and Lina’s explained review before any customer message was sent.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.text: I’ll explain the feedback before we send anything.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Good. The packet is ready.

comic.title: Lunch With Room to Breathe
comic.caption: The checked packet stayed upstairs with Lina as Mantas and Rūta went down to the café. They settled across from each other with bowls of soup. Eglė’s first morning was still a week away, leaving her time to finish her existing commitment. Rūta laid her notebook beside her bowl; there was no unfinished decision to carry into lunch. Mantas kept his phone in his pocket. Autumn light reached across the small table, and for a few minutes their attention rested on the meal and each other. Afterward, they would return to the ordinary afternoon work.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: Next Thursday is ready.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Then let’s enjoy lunch.

comic.title: The Shape of a Copy
comic.caption: After lunch, Mantas and Rūta returned upstairs. Lina had a fresh question waiting: a customer wanted to take a copy of their saved entries into a meeting away from the account screen. The old export note came back onto the table, but the request left an important gap. Did the customer need every entry, or only the entries matching a search? Rūta drew two small boxes on a fresh page. Lina prepared a short clarification, without promising a format or delivery date. For now, the work was to understand the need.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.text: They want a copy for a meeting.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Ask whether they need everything or just the search results.

comic.title: The Whole List
comic.caption: Lina sent the question while the three of them remained at the table. A few minutes later, the customer replied: the meeting needed all saved entries, including those outside the current search results. Rūta circled the complete-set sketch in her notebook. That settled which entries the request covered. Mantas suggested making a small paper sample with fictional entries next, so they could examine what a useful copy should contain. They had a clearer starting point, but had not chosen a file format or promised a delivery date. The export work remained deferred.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.text: They need every saved entry.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: Then this is the scope to examine.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Let’s try a paper sample first.

comic.title: Enough Context
comic.caption: Rūta laid two paper versions of the same invented set beside each other. The narrow version carried only names; the fuller one left room for the details already saved with each entry. Lina tried to use the sparse sheet as a meeting reference, then pointed to the fuller draft. A name could identify an entry without explaining what anyone was meant to discuss. Mantas held his pencil above the draft. They now had a concrete sample for checking useful contents with the customer, whose request covered the complete saved set. The papers were still fictional. A file format, a delivery date and an export feature remained undecided.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.text: The names tell me which entry, but not what we need to discuss.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Let’s check this fuller sample with them before choosing a format.

comic.title: Enough Context
comic.caption: Lina called the customer and described what the fuller fictional sheet kept: every saved entry name, followed by the details already belonging to it. She paused over the question that mattered—would that give the meeting enough context? The answer was yes, with the details left intact. Rūta moved the sparse version aside while Mantas bracketed the fuller groups in pencil. They now had a useful contents requirement, rather than a guess about what “a copy” meant. The papers remained examples; choosing a format and checking the work involved would come next.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.text: All entries, with the existing details left intact?

dialogue.speaker: Customer
dialogue.text: Yes. We need those details for the discussion.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Then let's check the format and effort before we promise a date.

comic.title: Keeping the Name With the Details
comic.caption: With the call finished, Darius came over to look at the proposed meeting copy. A long fictional entry ran onto a second sheet. In a compact row, its details lost their connection to the name above. Rūta moved the whole entry to a fresh sheet; Mantas marked where the name and its first details should stay together. They settled on grouped blocks for the next check, with room for a continuation when needed. Darius would try the longest fictional entries before estimating the effort. The contents were agreed, but a delivery date still had to wait.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: The name needs to travel with its details.

dialogue.speaker: Darius
dialogue.text: I’ll check the long examples before we estimate it.

comic.title: The Next Sheet
comic.caption: Darius tried an entry longer than a whole sheet. Starting it on a fresh page kept the name with its first details, but could not keep everything together. He spread the two pages across the table and marked the same fictional name at the start of the continuation. Lina followed the details from one sheet to the next; Rūta checked that nothing had disappeared between them. Mantas drew the distinction they needed: the name and beginning belonged together, while a longer entry needed a clear way to continue. The paper rule now held. Darius still had to assess the work before anyone could offer a delivery date.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.text: Now I can tell these two pages belong to the same entry.

dialogue.speaker: Darius
dialogue.text: I can use this rule to work out the effort.

comic.title: The Cost of a Page Break
comic.caption: Twenty minutes later, the laptop was open beside the two paper sheets. Darius had checked a local copy of the software with fictional entries. Reading the saved records was straightforward; arranging them for paper was a separate piece of work. The longer example would need careful page breaks, with its name repeated and every detail retained. He proposed a small local prototype, then checks with both short and long examples. Mantas agreed. The paper trial had settled what the copy should do. They would see how reliably it could do it before giving the customer a delivery estimate.

dialogue.speaker: Darius
dialogue.text: I can build a small prototype first.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: Then we’ll check both lengths against these sheets.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Let’s estimate delivery after those checks.

comic.title: A Clear Continuation
comic.caption: Forty minutes later, Darius turned the laptop toward the table. His local prototype kept the short example on one page and carried the longer example onto a second, repeating its name at the top. Rūta compared the preview with their fictional source sheets while Lina followed the continuation. Every existing detail remained, and each name stayed with the beginning of its entry. They recorded both checks. The paper convention now worked in a local preview. Before offering the customer an estimate, Darius still needed to assess connecting that layout to the account controls and arranging an independent check. Nothing had been exported from a customer account.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: The continuation is clear, and the details are all here.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Now tell us what remains before we give an estimate.

comic.title: The Whole Set
comic.caption: Darius turned from the layout to the route that would open it. They followed the existing account controls on a local diagram while Lina held a filtered fictional list beside the complete one. The customer’s request was for every saved name and its details, so the copy needed a whole-account scope even when search was active. Rūta wrote two checks: a filtered fictional account must produce its complete set; a different fictional account must remain separate. Darius now had a concrete integration plan. The layout success stood, but the team would check this route before giving a delivery estimate.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.text: All saved entries, even if the list is filtered.

dialogue.speaker: Darius
dialogue.text: The layout is ready. This route still needs wiring.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Build that path, then Rūta can check it.

comic.title: The Whole Set
comic.caption: Later that afternoon, Darius turned the laptop toward Rūta. The local copy route was ready for its first independent check. Using fictional entries, she narrowed the overview to one matching name, then opened the print layout. Lina kept the full comparison sheet beside the screen while Rūta checked every saved name and its existing details. The print view contained the complete current-account set; the search had changed only the overview. She marked that result in her notebook. A second fictional account still awaited its own check before the team could discuss an estimate.

dialogue.speaker: Darius
dialogue.text: The route is ready locally.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: The full set is here, with the details.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Now check the other account.

comic.title: A Separate Set
comic.caption: Rūta signed out of the first fictional account and opened the second. Lina laid its comparison sheet beside the laptop, keeping the first set apart. Every name and detail in the new print view belonged to the second account; none came from the first. Rūta returned to the first account and checked the reverse as well. The two sets stayed separate. She recorded the second independent pass. The local copy route had cleared its agreed checks, but the team still needed to review the remaining release work before Lina could give the customer an estimate.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: Each account keeps its own set.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Good. Now let’s review what remains before release.

comic.title: The Work Still Ahead
comic.caption: Beside Rūta’s completed local-check notebook, Darius drew three empty boxes on a fresh pad: prepare the deployment, verify the released route independently with fictional records, and write a short explanation for the customer. Rūta would compare the released copies with the same complete sets; Lina kept those sets apart while she took notes. Together they judged the remaining effort at about half a working day, provided the release checks passed. Mantas asked Lina to keep that condition beside the estimate. She recorded the work involved and left the delivery date open. The local result was encouraging. Availability still needed to be checked.

dialogue.speaker: Darius
dialogue.text: About half a working day, including the release checks.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Keep the checks beside the estimate.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.text: I’ll explain what remains before promising a date.

comic.title: Before the Release
comic.caption: The estimate became a practical sequence. Darius prepared the deployment package while Rūta put each fictional account’s reference sheets beside a fresh checklist. After release, she would compare every name and detail with its own set, then switch accounts and check the separation again. Mantas agreed that a mismatch would stop acceptance. Lina drafted a short explanation of the work still underway, leaving availability unconfirmed. The plan was ready; the release and its independent checks were still ahead. No customer message had gone out.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: If either account shows the wrong entries, we stop.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: I’ll compare each released view with its own sheet.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.text: I’ll keep availability unconfirmed until those checks pass.

comic.title: The Final Comparison
comic.caption: Darius deployed the prepared route. Rūta opened the released print views for two fictional accounts and compared them against her separate reference sets. Even with a narrow search still active, every saved name and detail appeared. The short record stayed on one page; the longer record continued on a second, keeping its name with the beginning and repeating it on the continuation. Each account contained only its own entries. Rūta marked the last box. Mantas accepted the results, and Lina revised her unsent guidance to reflect verified availability. The customer's own data remained untouched.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: Both references match. The accounts stay separate.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Good. Let’s review the instructions before Lina sends them.

comic.title: Instructions Sent
comic.caption: Lina placed her draft beside the fictional account. Following its steps, Rūta reached the complete view and checked that the narrow search had not shortened the copy. They shortened one sentence and made the last step explicit: use the complete account view when saving or printing. Mantas approved the wording. Lina sent the reviewed instructions herself, asking the customer to confirm whether their resulting copy contained all their saved names and details. The route was available; the customer’s own result was still unknown.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: The last step should say which view to save.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: That’s clear. Send it.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.text: Sent. I’ve asked them to check the full copy.

comic.title: The Customer’s Copy
comic.caption: A little later that Thursday afternoon, Lina paused with her hand above the keyboard. The customer had replied: they had saved their own whole-account copy and checked it against their account; every saved name and detail was present. Lina read the confirmation aloud. Mantas closed his notebook, and Rūta gathered the fictional pages used for the checks. The task could finally leave the follow-up list. Their evidence now included the customer's own result, without anyone at the office opening that account or handling its contents. Eglė's first morning was still a week away.

dialogue.speaker: Lina
dialogue.text: They checked their own copy. All the names and details are there.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Good. We can close this follow-up.

comic.title: The Way Home
comic.caption: By the end of Thursday’s workday, the fictional test pages were put away and the customer follow-up was closed. Eglė’s first-morning packet was ready for next week. Mantas pulled a dark jacket over his teal sweater and went downstairs with Rūta. Outside, the pavement held the cool smell of fallen leaves. Rūta stopped by the doorway to say goodbye. Along the curb, Mantas’s bus was approaching. He turned toward the stop, letting the finished day stay upstairs. His running kit was waiting at home.

dialogue.speaker: Rūta
dialogue.text: See you tomorrow.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: See you. My bus is coming.

comic.title: The Ride Home
comic.caption: Mantas let the departing passengers clear the doorway, then stepped aboard. A few minutes later he had a window seat, and the office corner slipped behind the bus. Amber lamps stretched across the damp street; autumn branches passed between him and the buildings. His phone stayed in his pocket. The customer had their complete copy, and the follow-up was closed. For the length of this journey, there was nothing he needed to answer. He sat back and let the city carry him home.

comic.title: The Hallway Light
comic.caption: The bus carried Mantas through the last of the evening traffic. From his stop, the walk home was short enough for the cool air to clear the warmth of the carriage. He let himself in, set down his bag and keys, and lifted his jacket onto its peg. The phone stayed in its pocket. Beyond the hallway, the kitchen waited under a warm light. He had reached the ordinary end of a full day; now he could make himself supper.

comic.title: A Small Supper
comic.caption: In the kitchen, Mantas set a bowl beside the bread board and put mushrooms and onions into the pan. The first quiet hiss of supper replaced the sounds of the bus and street. He stirred slowly, watching the onions soften while the window gathered the blue of the October evening. There was enough time to let the food cook properly. The customer’s follow-up was finished, and the next working day could wait. For now, the task in front of him was small and complete: warm food, a place at the table, and an evening at home.

comic.title: A Warm Bowl
comic.caption: The onions had softened and the mushrooms had browned. Mantas turned off the hob, filled the waiting bowl and carried it to the table with the dark bread. He sat down and lifted his first mouthful while the kitchen was still warm from cooking. Beyond the window, the October evening deepened. His phone stayed in the jacket pocket in the hallway. For a little while, the next thing to do was simply eat.

comic.title: The Last Dish
comic.caption: Supper took as long as it needed. Mantas finished the mushrooms and onions, carried the empty bowl to the sink and cleared the table. Warm water loosened the last traces of the meal; the pan was already washed and set aside. Beyond the kitchen window, the blue of the evening had deepened over Vilnius. He rinsed the bowl, feeling his shoulders drop. The day’s customer question had an answer, and Eglė’s first morning was still a week away. For now, there was only this small task to finish, then an evening to himself.

comic.title: A Quiet Page
comic.caption: The last bowl rested on the draining rack, and the tap was silent. Mantas left the kitchen ready for morning and carried a book to the armchair. Under the lamp, he found his place and began to read. The warm windows across Vilnius were small against the deepening blue outside. There was no next decision waiting on this page, no reply to prepare before he turned it. Supper was finished, the day’s work was closed, and his phone stayed in the jacket in the hallway. For a while, the evening could move at the pace of a sentence.

comic.title: The Saved Place
comic.caption: At the end of the chapter, Mantas slipped a plain bookmark between the pages and laid the closed book on the low table. The evening had become quiet enough to hear the room itself: the small sounds of the building, the faint movement of traffic below. He rose and switched off the reading lamp. Light from the kitchen still reached the chair; beyond the window, Vilnius glimmered blue and gold. His place in the book would wait. It was time to sleep.

comic.title: A Quiet End
comic.caption: Mantas left the closed book on the low table and went through to the bedroom. He changed for bed, folded his sweater and trousers on the chair, and set his shoes beneath it. The apartment had settled into its evening quiet. The customer follow-up was closed, and Eglė’s first morning was still a week away. He eased under the duvet and reached for the bedside lamp. Tomorrow could begin after a night’s sleep.

comic.title: Friday Light
comic.caption: The lamp went dark, and Thursday ended. Mantas slept through the night. By the time pale Friday light reached the window, the room had cooled from amber to blue-grey. He pushed the duvet back and sat on the edge of the bed, bare feet resting on the rug, giving himself a moment to wake fully. The folded clothes were still on the chair; the phone was still in the hallway jacket. Yesterday’s customer follow-up was closed. This morning could begin at an ordinary pace.

comic.title: Water Before the Trail
comic.caption: Mantas got up and brought his stored running kit out for Friday's long run. In the kitchen, pale light had reached the counter. He set the hydration vest on a dry patch beside the sink and held the first flask beneath the tap; the second waited within reach. The familiar preparations gave the morning a shape: water first, then his phone from the hallway jacket, then the trail. He would take the woodland route at an easy pace. For now, he watched the flask fill.

comic.title: Ready to Go
comic.caption: Mantas filled the second flask, closed the tap and settled both bottles into his vest. In the hallway, yesterday’s jacket gave back his phone; he zipped it away and picked up his keys. A final tug on the vest straps was enough. He stepped onto the quiet landing and drew the apartment door after him, leaving the kitchen and its small pool of dawn light behind. The long run would begin gently. There was no need to spend the morning’s calm before he reached the trees.

comic.title: First Bus
comic.caption: The key turned, and Mantas checked the door once before heading downstairs. Outside, the cool air woke him fully. He walked the familiar few streets to the bus stop, keeping the start of his long run easy before it had even begun. By the shelter he zipped his keys away with his phone. A bus rolled toward him through the pale morning light. He stayed back from the kerb, watching it slow, while the city began its Friday around him.

comic.title: A Seat by the Window
comic.caption: The bus drew level with the shelter and stopped. Mantas boarded and took a seat by the window, keeping the aisle clear. As it pulled away, the houses and yellow birches began to pass through the glass. His phone and keys stayed zipped inside the vest; there was nothing he needed to check before the trail. He let his hands rest on his thighs and watched the morning light reach the upper windows. The familiar woodland lay ahead along the route. For now, the journey gave him a few quiet minutes before the long run.

comic.title: Into the Morning Woods
comic.caption: The buildings thinned, and the familiar belt of woodland appeared beside the road. At the woodland-edge stop, Mantas stepped onto the pavement and followed the short pedestrian link to the trailhead. By his first easy strides, the bus was already moving away. Cool shade gathered beneath the birches and pines, while sunlight caught the gold leaves above him. He let the opening minutes stay gentle, giving his legs time to warm. Both flasks were filled; his phone and keys stayed zipped away. The long run had begun.

comic.title: Among the Roots
comic.caption: A few minutes beyond the trailhead, roots spread across the path, some hidden beneath fallen leaves. Mantas shortened his stride, then let the run become a brisk walk across the uneven stretch. This morning was for distance at an easy effort; there was no reason to force the pace on uncertain footing. He placed each orange shoe on firm earth between the roots, breathing evenly beneath the pines. The trail continued through the birches, and he would return to an easy jog once he was clear of the rough patch.

comic.title: Room to Run
comic.caption: Beyond the last thick roots, the trail widened into a bend of firm earth. Mantas let his brisk walk become a gentle jog, keeping the first strides short until the rhythm felt easy again. His shoulders settled; he looked along the path instead of down at every step. The rough patch had cost him a little time, but there was no reason to earn it back. He followed the curve between the birches and pines, orange shoes lifting clear of the scattered leaves. The long run could continue at its own pace.

comic.title: The Longer Branch
comic.caption: A few minutes beyond the smoother bend, the path divided. Mantas knew the left branch: it would bring him back around the short return loop. Today he had left enough time for the longer circuit. He let his stride shorten through the fork, checked the ground ahead, and turned right. The trees drew closer around that path, softening the morning light. There was no reason to accelerate now that the footing was firmer. He settled into the same easy rhythm and carried on.

comic.title: A Drink on the Rise
comic.caption: Beyond the fork, the longer trail rose steadily between the birches. Mantas shortened his stride on the climb and let the pace settle. At the top of the modest rise, he found a level patch of firm earth and paused for a small drink. The second flask stayed in his vest; his phone and keys stayed zipped away. Early light caught the leaves beside the path, which curved onward through the pines. He could feel the climb in his breathing, but there was no need to hurry. A moment here, then the circuit would continue.

comic.title: An Easy Descent
comic.caption: Mantas settled the flask back into its pocket and eased into a jog. Beyond the rise, the longer circuit curved down through birches and pines. Damp leaves lay along the edges, with clear earth between the roots. He shortened his stride and looked a few paces ahead, letting the slope set a gentler rhythm. The minute spent drinking needed no compensation. With both flasks secure and his hands free, he followed the bend into the trees, breathing evenly as the morning light reached farther across the path.

comic.title: The Firm Edge
comic.caption: Beyond the curve, the trail settled into a shallow hollow. A puddle spread across its middle, holding a few brown leaves and a pale reflection of the birches. Mantas eased out of his jog before reaching it. There was firm earth along the side, wide enough for an ordinary walking step. He kept his eyes on that margin and walked beside the water without trying to jump it. The small pause cost him nothing he needed to recover. Both flasks stayed secured in his vest, and the longer circuit continued ahead through the trees.

comic.title: Clear Ground
comic.caption: A few careful walking steps brought Mantas past the far end of the puddle. On the clear earth beyond it, he eased back into a jog. The trail rose gently out of the hollow, its wet leaves thinning between the pines and birches. He let the first strides stay short until his footing felt settled, then returned to the comfortable rhythm he had held before the descent. The water was behind him; the longer circuit still lay ahead. There was no lost time to make up.

comic.title: At the Crest
comic.caption: The rise eased onto a level stretch. Mantas slowed, then stopped at the firm edge of the trail where the pines opened a little. Across the hollow, the first sunlight touched the autumn leaves while a thin mist lingered between the trunks. He stood for a few breaths, letting the view catch up with him. The trail curved onward through the trees, and there was still plenty of the longer circuit ahead. He could continue at the same easy pace after this small pause.

comic.title: Across the Track
comic.caption: Mantas turned from the hollow and settled back into his easy rhythm. A few minutes farther along, the narrow trail met a sandy forestry track. He slowed, looked along it in both directions and walked across toward the footpath on the other side. Old tire impressions held a scattering of birch leaves; the track itself was quiet. There was no reason to hurry through the crossing. Beyond it, the familiar longer circuit continued between the trees, and he could return to his comfortable pace.

comic.title: Room to Pass
comic.caption: On the far side of the forestry track, Mantas found his easy rhythm again. A few minutes farther along the narrow footpath, a loose birch branch lay across the walking line. He slowed to a walk and stopped on firm ground. Taking its dry end, he guided it onto the mossy verge, well clear of the trail. It needed only a moment; the next person would have room to pass without stepping into the undergrowth. The walking line was open again. Mantas was ready to straighten and continue along the longer circuit through the quiet morning woods.

comic.title: Back Into Rhythm
comic.caption: Mantas straightened, left the birch branch on the moss and set off again. The first few strides were short and easy; then his breathing settled into the familiar pace. Low morning sunlight caught the autumn leaves along the curving footpath. He kept his pace comfortable, with no reason to make up the moment spent clearing the way. The branch now lay beyond the walking line. Ahead of him, the longer circuit continued through the quiet forest, and he settled back into the run.

comic.title: Room to Pass
comic.caption: Beyond the curve, a cyclist was walking his bicycle up the narrow path. Mantas eased out of his jog and stepped onto firm moss beside the trail. The rider kept the wheels on the clear strip of earth, leaving the ferns undisturbed. They exchanged a brief nod as the bicycle came through. Mantas waited with his hands relaxed, ready to step back once the rear wheel had passed. A few quiet seconds gave them both room; his steady run could carry on from here.

dialogue.speaker: Mantas
dialogue.text: Go ahead.

dialogue.speaker: Cyclist
dialogue.text: Thanks.

comic.title: Back into Stride
comic.caption: Mantas waited until the bicycle’s rear wheel had passed, then stepped from the firm moss onto the clear trail. The cyclist continued uphill behind him. A few easy strides brought back the rhythm of the run: feet light on the leaf-strewn earth, breath even, eyes on the next stretch. He let the brief pause remain a pause, without trying to make up its seconds. Morning light reached between the pines as the path carried him farther along the longer circuit. There was room now to run at his own comfortable pace.

comic.title: The Homeward Bend
comic.caption: A few minutes beyond the cyclist, the path dipped toward a shallow stream. Mantas recognized the low wooden bridge: from here, the longer circuit would curve back toward the woodland edge. A thin shine of moisture lay across the planks. He let his stride shorten, then settled into a walk. The stream slipped quietly beneath him as he kept his steps measured. There was time to take this crossing at its own pace. Beyond the bridge, the clear path continued between the birches.

comic.title: The Far Bank
comic.caption: On the far bank, Mantas walked a few more steps until the damp planks were behind him. The return path was firm and clear, with enough room to find his comfortable rhythm again. He eased back into a jog. The little bridge receded between the trunks while the shallow stream followed its own course below the mossy bank. There was no reason to make up the seconds spent walking; he still had the rest of the familiar return trail ahead.

comic.title: The Last Stretch
comic.caption: About ten minutes beyond the stream, the trees began to thin and the return path opened into the familiar woodland-edge trailhead. Mantas let his final easy strides settle into a walk. The longer circuit was complete: a drink after the climb, careful steps over the wet ground, room for another trail user, and an unhurried crossing of the bridge. Now he could simply catch his breath. His flasks stayed secured in the vest; the bus home was the next part of the morning.

comic.title: The Homeward Bus
comic.caption: A few minutes of gentle walking settled Mantas’s breathing. He followed the pavement from the woodland edge to the bus stop, the morning light still low through the birches. When the bus drew in and stopped beside the curb, he stepped through the open door with a hand on the rail. The longer circuit was finished; there was no reason to hurry the journey home. His flasks stayed secured in the vest, and his phone and keys remained zipped away. Breakfast and a shower could wait until he reached his flat.

comic.title: Kit by the Door
comic.caption: The bus brought Mantas back into the city, and a short walk took him to his own door. He unlocked it, stepped inside and set his orange shoes on the tray. Now he lifted the vest onto its hook, both flasks still secured in their pockets. The phone could stay zipped away a little longer; his keys were on the shelf. The longer circuit was finished, and he had returned without hurrying the wet sections. A shower and breakfast were next, before the working day began.

atlas.title: The Ammonite Mere
